s1.title: Overview of Official Development Assistance
s1.p1: Official Development Assistance (ODA) is a programme involving Multinational Organisations (OECD, UN, IMF, AFD, AU…) and supported and financed by Western States. It constitutes all grants and financing granted by the world's wealthiest powers to countries in difficulty. Aid amounting to several billion dollars, whose donor countries are (the United States, Germany, the United Kingdom, Japan, France).
s1.q2: What is the Mission of ODA?
s1.p2: The primary mission of the ODA programme is to promote the economic development of third-world countries, by directing the various funds collected towards the implementation of concrete and sustainable projects, essential infrastructure, actions to combat hunger, health, education, etc.
s1.p3: The ODA programme is directed by the DAC (Development Assistance Committee) composed of the representative body of the Organisations and States involved in the programme.
s2.title: Some facts about ODA
fig.caption: ODA/APD
s2.p1a: ODA from members of the Development Assistance Committee (DAC), boosted by additional expenditure mobilised to help developing countries, reached a high level of USD 161.2 billion, representing an increase of 3.5% in real terms. Bilateral ODA destined for Africa and the least developed countries increased by 4.1% and 1.8% respectively. Humanitarian aid increased by 6%.
s2.p1b: Excluding aid devoted to hosting refugees in donor countries — which recorded a decline of 9.5% to USD 9.0 billion, mainly attributable to Canada, Iceland and the Netherlands — ODA increased by 4.4% in real terms.
s2.h2: ODA balances the instability of Developing Countries
s2.p2a: Financing projects, improving access to water, healthcare and quality education, protecting biodiversity or combating climate disruption: these are all essential objectives, both for the populations of developing countries and for international stability. However, such objectives do not always interest public and private investors, who consider them too risky or even non-priority. "International finance generally goes very little to low-income countries and social sectors", notes Hubert de Milly, ODA expert at the French Development Agency (AFD).
s2.p2b: And this is where official development assistance comes into play. By filling the lack of financing in certain neglected sectors and areas — through grants, loans or other forms of support — it makes it possible to drive change for the most vulnerable populations. Often, it even brings with it other actors — banks, companies, foundations — thus increasing the sums devoted to development.
s2.p3: ODA makes it possible to initiate projects in neglected sectors or areas. It initiates virtuous development logics and creates dynamics capable of bringing in all other actors, notably companies. It creates a leverage effect that multiplies impacts. In total, since the 1960s, development aid has demonstrated its effectiveness: it is a powerful factor of change for the most vulnerable populations. This aid can relate to local projects or very large-scale policies at country level over the long term.
s3.title: Census of Agents within the Programme
s3.p1: ODA, through its actions, directs part of this financing into the launching of development projects across African States. An action that takes into account the realities and difficulties encountered by Country.
s3.p2: To this end, ODA requires and carries out a census, by African State, of Agents for the proper functioning and monitoring of the various projects to be executed.
s3.p3: Adult Citizens of Africa residing in their Countries or in the Diaspora, are therefore invited without distinction of professional qualifications, and without age limit, to subscribe to the Programme in the interest of contributing to the execution of various Projects or Social Actions, which will be directed towards their Nations.
s4.title: Missions
s4.r1li1: Represents the Liaison Agent between his State and the Programme Committee.
s4.r1li3: Directs Assistants on Project Implementation Tasks.
s4.r1li4: Carries out project progress reports to the Programme Committee.
s4.r2li1: Under the orders of the Representative Agent.
s4.r2li2: Constitute the Field Agents of the Representative.
s4.r2li3: Will be distributed by Activity Sector according to qualification.
s4.r2li4: Report to the Representative on the progress of tasks according to their Activity Sectors.
s5.title: Privileges for participants
s5.li2: Maturing Experience and Broadening Professional Relationships.
s5.li3: Social Security Coverage (Family Health Insurance, Family Allowances, End-of-Contract Pension, Professional Risk Insurance).
s5.li4: Company vehicle + Mission and housing allowances.
s6.title: Conditions and Criteria
s6.li1: People sought: All Educated Adults wishing to apply. (Integration training is given before taking up the position).
s6.li3: Contract duration: 7-year fixed-term contract (To complete the Projects).
s6.li4: Nature: Part-time offers but paid monthly, not requiring participants to interrupt their personal occupations. (Parallel sources of profitability).
s6.li5: Place of Work: The participant works for his country in projects directed towards that destination. However, he may also work internationally if he so wishes.
s6.li6: Offers also valid for Retirees or Diaspora participants.
